However, I soon realized the grave mistake I had made in underestimating the spread of slavery and the moral imperative to oppose it.

When I saw the consequences of that decision unfolding before me, I did not shy away from admitting my error. I publicly spoke out against the act and dedicated myself to the cause of opposing the extension of slavery into new territories. I learned from that experience that political expediency should never come at the cost of compromising one's principles.
